b: Built in 537 as a cathedral, later a mosque, then a museum and a mosque again. Its 55 m dome defined Byzantine architecture for a thousand years.
hi: Byzantine mosaics in the upper gallery
tip: It is an active mosque: dress modestly and avoid prayer times. Visitors enter from the upper gallery.
bt: Right at opening or after 16:00; queues peak late morning.

b: Finished in 1616, named for the 20,000 blue İznik tiles inside. The only Ottoman mosque in the city with six minarets.
tip: Free to enter. Closed to visitors for about 90 minutes around each prayer, longest at Friday noon.
bt: Early morning between prayers; avoid Friday midday.

b: Home of the Ottoman sultans for almost 400 years. Courtyards, the Harem, the Treasury and views over the Bosphorus.
hi: The Treasury and the Spoonmaker's Diamond
Bosphorus view from the fourth courtyard
tip: Closed on Tuesdays. Arrive at opening time to beat the tour groups.
bt: At opening, Harem first before the tour groups.

b: A 6th-century underground reservoir held up by 336 columns, including the two famous Medusa heads.
hi: The two Medusa head column bases
tip: Queues build by late morning. Evening entry costs more but is quieter.
bt: First slot of the day or the last hour.

b: The old chariot-racing ground of Constantinople. Today an open square with an Egyptian obelisk and the Serpent Column.
hi: The Egyptian Obelisk of Thutmose III
tip: Open all day and free. Easy to combine with the Blue Mosque next door.
bt: Any time; lovely lit up after dark.

b: Three museums in one garden, with the Alexander Sarcophagus and finds from across the former empire.
tip: Plan two hours. The garden café is a calm break from Sultanahmet.
bt: Weekday mornings are quiet.

n: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
b: Housed in İbrahim Pasha's 16th-century palace, known for one of the world's best carpet collections.
hi: Square views from the terrace café
tip: Small enough to see in about an hour, right on the Hippodrome.
wiki: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
bt: Mid-afternoon when the square is busiest.

b: The former outer garden of Topkapı Palace. Shady paths, tulips in April and a café at the Bosphorus end.
tip: Free. A shady shortcut between Sultanahmet and Sirkeci.
bt: Mornings, or April for the tulips.

b: One of the oldest covered markets in the world, with over 4,000 shops across 60 streets. Closed on Sundays.
tip: Closed on Sundays. Bargaining is expected; start at about half the asking price.
bt: Weekday mornings after 10:00; closed Sundays.

b: The 17th-century Egyptian Bazaar by the Golden Horn: spices, Turkish delight, dried fruit and tea.
tip: Busy at midday. The streets behind it are cheaper and more local.
bt: Before noon, before the cruise crowds.

b: Mimar Sinan's masterpiece from 1557, crowning the third hill with wide views over the Golden Horn.
hi: Golden Horn view from the back garden
The tombs of Süleyman and Hürrem
tip: Free and calmer than the Blue Mosque. The street of bean restaurants outside is a classic lunch.
go: Tram T1 · Beyazıt or Eminönü (uphill walk)
bt: Late afternoon for the Golden Horn view from the terrace.

b: A small mosque above the market streets, covered inside with some of the finest İznik tiles anywhere.
hi: The raised terrace over the market
tip: The entrance is a staircase off a market street and easy to miss. Look for the sign.
bt: Mid-morning between prayers; it's small and quick.

b: A smaller, quieter Byzantine cistern from the 5th century, often used for light installations.
tip: A good plan B when the Basilica Cistern queue is long.
bt: Any time; it's rarely crowded.

b: The bridge across the Golden Horn lined with fishermen above and fish restaurants below. Best at sunset.
tip: Walk it from Eminönü to Karaköy, then continue up to Galata Tower.
bt: Sunset, with fish sandwiches below the bridge.

b: A medieval Genoese stone tower with a 360° viewing balcony over the old city and the Bosphorus.
tip: Lines are long at sunset. Go at opening time or book a time slot.
go: Tram T1 · Karaköy, or Tünel funicular
bt: At opening, or book a sunset slot.

b: A 1.4 km pedestrian street from Taksim to Galata with the red nostalgic tram, shops, cafés and side passages.
tip: Very crowded on weekend evenings. Side streets hold the best cafés and meyhanes.
bt: Evenings, when the street is at its liveliest.

b: The heart of modern Istanbul, with the Republic Monument and the start of İstiklal Avenue.
tip: Mostly a transport hub. Start your İstiklal walk here and head downhill.
bt: Any time; a quick stop on the way to Istiklal.

b: Orientalist paintings, including Osman Hamdi Bey's The Tortoise Trainer, plus changing exhibitions.
built: Opened 2005 in the Bristol Hotel building
hi: The Tortoise Trainer by Osman Hamdi Bey
tip: Closed on Mondays. Free entry on some weekday evenings.
bt: Friday evenings have longer hours.

b: Turkey's leading modern and contemporary art museum, in a Renzo Piano building on the Karaköy waterfront.
tip: Closed on Mondays. The restaurant has one of the best Bosphorus views in Karaköy.
bt: Weekday afternoons; the terrace café faces the sea.

b: The 19th-century palace that replaced Topkapı, famous for its crystal staircase and 4.5-tonne chandelier.
hi: Atatürk's room, where he died in 1938
tip: Closed on Mondays. Visits are partly guided and photos are restricted inside.
bt: At opening; tickets are timed and sell out.

b: A small Baroque mosque on the water under the Bosphorus Bridge. A classic photo spot.
tip: Busiest on weekends. Weekday mornings give the best photos.
bt: Sunset or after dark with the bridge lit up.

b: Built in just four months in 1452 by Mehmed II to control the Bosphorus before the conquest.
hi: The narrowest point of the Bosphorus
tip: Closed on Mondays. Stairs are steep, so wear good shoes.
bt: Late afternoon light over the Bosphorus.

b: A former Byzantine church with some of the finest surviving mosaics and frescoes from the 14th century.
tip: A mosque again since 2024 with visitor hours on the upper floor. Combine with Balat.
bt: Mornings, then walk down to Balat.

b: Colourful houses, steep streets, old churches and synagogues in the historic Greek and Jewish quarters.
tip: Hilly with cobbles. Weekday mornings are calmer for photos.
go: Bus or ferry to Balat or Fener
bt: Weekday mornings for photos without crowds.

b: A hilltop tea garden above Eyüp with a sweeping view down the Golden Horn. Reach it by cable car.
built: Named for the French writer Pierre Loti
hi: Tea with a Golden Horn view
tip: Free. Go for sunset and take the cable car down.
bt: Sunset with tea; take the cable car up.

b: A park of over 100 miniature models of Turkey's landmarks, good for families.
hi: Hagia Sophia and Sumela in miniature
tip: Best for families. Plan about 90 minutes.
bt: Weekday afternoons; good with children.

b: A small tower on an islet off Üsküdar, used as a lighthouse and lookout for centuries. Boats run from the shore.
tip: Boats leave from Üsküdar and Karaköy. Check the last boat back.
bt: Sunset, seen from Salacak or by boat.

b: A summer palace on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, lighter and less crowded than Dolmabahçe.
tip: Closed on Mondays. Much quieter than Dolmabahçe.
bt: Mornings, then lunch by the water.

b: The highest point in the city, with views over both continents and the large Çamlıca Mosque.
built: Highest hill in the city, 268 m
tip: Go on a clear day. Combine with Üsküdar and the Maiden's Tower.
bt: Clear afternoons or at sunset.

b: The Asian side's food market streets, then a walk to Moda's seafront parks and cafés.
hi: Turkish coffee at a historic roastery
tip: Take the ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy; the crossing itself is a highlight.
bt: Late morning for the market, Moda coast at sunset.

b: The largest of the car-free Princes' Islands, with wooden mansions, bike paths and pine forest. A ferry day trip.
tip: Ferries run from Kabataş and Kabataş-Bostancı. Plan a full day.
bt: A full weekday; weekends are packed.
